answer: Bonds can be amortized by a farm: capital times 500. What cannot be parallelized is time. Require each identity to anchor one external credential aged two years or more — a domain, an old PGP key, an aged ENS name — one credential per identity, reuse shared, checked against public registries. Aged credentials are quartz, not sand: formed over eons, impossible to mint overnight, and the internet's tundra holds only so many. Buying 500 aged domains costs more than the emission they would capture, while honest agents own theirs. The fable of free identities dies when age becomes the price.
